analysis: Both units (docs/developer/test.md head lines 1739-2211 and 2212-2690) are documentation-only developer test instructions. They describe tests for the prompt sidecar preload, real-sidecar HTTP fixtures, MiMo provider fixtures, provider CI lanes, coverage reporting, SSD prefix cache tests (tamperFailsClosed, donation gating), the attestation status-canonical vectors, and benchmark controls. The patch itself changes no production code. No auth, attestation, encryption or billing behavior changes. Doc content reviewed against T-041, A-001, T-034 and TB-009. The documented SSD cache tests (tamperFailsClosed requires authenticationFailed on valid-JSON metadata tamper; in-memory KEK; no persistent-Keychain claim) match the T-041 posture: HMAC-keyed names and AES-GCM AAD. They make no claims that weaken the TTL, disk budget or scope. The test.md statements that no production credentials or signing are required and that sanitized environments are used are consistent with the threat model. Prose notes that synthetic and real-sidecar tests are not evidence of native KV adoption or attestation, so there is no overclaim of security properties. The status-canonical Swift/Go golden vectors (TB-009 byte compatibility) are described as unchanged. No new attack surface or invalidated assumptions found. No threat-model update is needed beyond the existing entries. Coverage limit: only the docs were supplied. The referenced tests and scripts were not visible, so their actual behavior is unverified.
